description: Downloads on first use (site/js/lazy.js, fetch=lazy) against everything before the shell starts (fetch=all), on the unkernel engine. 2026-11-23, a laptop (AMD Zen 4) on a home connection that gave 10 to 17 MB/s from cache.nixos.org, headless Chromium 157 with SwiftShader WebGL, viewport 1280x1000. Each run boots `?pkg=<name>&engine=unkernel&fetch=<mode>&boot=1` in a fresh browser profile (run "cold": empty Cache API), then once more in the same profile (run "warm"), types its command the moment the shell is ready, and waits for the command's closing line (hello; jj --version; python3 -c 'import json'; page clock, as tools/exec-bench.py times it) or the compositor's first frame from the program (sol from aisleriot; es2gears_wayland from mesa-demos, with the site's GL driver; firefox). Runs with round "prime" are one untimed fetch=all boot of each case so the CDN's edge held every NAR; the timed rounds swap the order of the two modes. `build` is the commit the site was built from: ae0224ce fetches through ELF headers and references of 2 MiB or less; 18a0294a also starts references largest first (the docs' numbers: fetch=lazy from it, fetch=all pooled from both, which run the same code); "prefetching off" is 18a0294a with neither ELF headers nor references followed; 52ea2333 followed every reference of a touched path. shell_s: navigation to the prompt (host clock, 50 ms poll). first_output_s: typing to the output or first frame. at_shell, at_output, settled: window.trynix.downloads() at the prompt, at the output, and once reading had stopped for 8 s; streamedBytes counts compressed bytes read, from the network on a cold run and from the Cache API on a warm one. timeline, kept for some runs: the store's events on the page's clock in ms: demand or prefetch when a path is asked for, start, written, and touch at the guest's first lookup inside a path (ready: whether it had arrived by then). Some cold runs met a slow network (python3 fetch=lazy round 1 of ae0224ce: a 59 MiB NAR took 30 s), which is why the docs give medians.
